review.tagline: Converts books and document folders into on-demand agent skills with per-chapter files
review.summary: A Python extractor turns PDF, EPUB, DOCX, Markdown, HTML, RTF or MOBI files into clean text. The agent then follows SKILL.md to generate a skill: a core SKILL.md, one file per chapter, a glossary, patterns and a cheatsheet. The skill installs under ~/.agents/skills/ and loads chapters on demand in Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode or OpenClaw. The README reports 24x–51x fewer tokens than dumping the book into context.
review.audience: Developers who want agents to answer from technical books or internal docs
strengths: Reads PDF, EPUB, DOCX, MD, HTML, RTF and MOBI, with fallbacks to stdlib parsers
One SKILL.md output works across seven agent hosts that follow the Agent Skills format
Chapter files load only when asked, keeping the base skill near 4,000 tokens
Extraction runs locally; `extract.py --check` reports which extractors are missing
weaknesses: Scanned PDFs are rejected; OCR (for example ocrmypdf) must be run first
Generation quality depends on the host agent and its model, not the extractor
Sharing skills built from copyrighted books can infringe; README advises keeping them private
needs: Needs Python 3, pdftotext (poppler), docling, pypdf, ebooklib, beautifulsoup4, python-docx, Calibre ebook-convert, ocrmypdf
Models: Any model in the host agent (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, OpenClaw)
